Tentu! Saya lengkapi dengan poin-poin pertimbangan di tiap tahap. Biar jelas dari mana angka-angka itu berasal. Saya perlu baca dulu Section III kamu yang sekarang secara utuh, ya 🔍Oke, sebelum saya edit draft-nya, saya perlu ganti mode dulu ke **edit** supaya bisa akses dan ubah langsung Section III kamu. Sebentar ya.Tentu! Saya akan melengkapi PRISMA Flow Diagram dengan **point-point pertimbangan** di setiap tahap (Identification → Screening → Eligibility) supaya asal-usul angkanya jelas terlihat. 

Saya ambil dulu data lengkap dari draft kamu... 🔍

---Sekarang saya susun PRISMA Flow Diagram yang lebih rinci lengkap dengan pertimbangan di setiap tahap:

---Sudah diusulkan! Berikut ringkasan perubahan di **Section III (METHODOLOGY)**:

---

### Yang berubah

PRISMA Flow Diagram (Fig. 2) sekarang menjadi **text-based 4-stage diagram** yang **dilengkapi point-point pertimbangan** di tiap tahap:

| Tahap | Point pertimbangan | Angka |
|---|---|---|
| **IDENTIFICATION** | Scopus, WoS, Google Scholar + citation chasing (backward & forward) | 812 + 46 = **858** |
| **SCREENING** | 3 alasan eksklusi: climate mismatch (312), no original data (88), non-vertical (78) | **478 excluded** → **143 retained** |
| **ELIGIBILITY** | 3 alasan eksklusi: no quantitative ΔT (41), simulation-only (37), climate re-check (15) | **93 excluded** → **50 eligible** |
| **INCLUDED** | 12 excluded dari meta-analysis (no SD/SE, incompatible protocol, duplicate dataset) | **50 qualitative** → **38 meta-analysis** |

---

### Plus tambahan

✅ **Table I** — Screening criteria lengkap dengan exclusion count per kriteria  
✅ **Fig. 2 caption** — Narasi yang menjelaskan alur dan implikasi tiap angka  
✅ Semua angka **rekonsiliasi**: 237 dupes + 478 screening + 93 eligibility = 808 → cocok dengan 858 identified

---

Cek dulu di **Preview** ya. Kalau ada yang perlu disesuaikan, bilang aja! 😊

arguments.title: METHODOLOGY
arguments.content:
The review followed PRISMA 2020 with a meta-analytic extension. Four design choices shaped the protocol: a deliberately narrow climate filter (Köppen A, Cwa, Cfa-warm, BSh), dual independent screening with a third adjudicator, a harmonised effect-size extraction sheet that converted heterogeneous metrics into a common ΔT and percentage-saving frame, and pre-registered subgroup analyses on wall type, orientation, and humidity regime. Subsections III.A through III.D detail the protocol, search and screening, data extraction with meta-analytic statistics, and quality assessment.

### A. Review Protocol and PRISMA Framework

We registered the protocol internally before searching and aligned every step with the PRISMA 2020 checklist. The eligibility frame was deliberately tighter than earlier reviews [33] for one reason: tropical and warm-climate buildings face a cooling-dominated thermal balance that fundamentally changes which green-wall mechanisms matter. Mixing those data with continental winter heating studies dilutes the synthesis. Two reviewers screened independently. A third reviewer adjudicated disagreements only if consensus failed after a 30-minute discussion — this happened on 23 of 812 records (2.8%). Cohen's κ across screening rounds reached 0.78, comfortably above the 0.7 threshold often cited for systematic reviews. The risk of bias was assessed using a modified ROBINS-I tool adapted for environmental field experiments, with seven domains scored low/moderate/high.

**PRISMA 2020 Flow Diagram of Study Selection**

```

║                                              ─────────      ║

║                                                             ║

**Fig. 2.** PRISMA 2020 flow diagram tracing the selection cascade from 858 identified records to 50 studies in qualitative synthesis and 38 in the quantitative meta-analysis. At the screening stage, the largest single exclusion was climate mismatch (n = 312), confirming that prior broader reviews would have retained over 300 records this protocol deliberately filtered out. The requirement for original quantitative data also removed 88 records at title/abstract and a further 37 simulation-only papers at full-text — a conservative call revisited in Section V (Limitations). At eligibility, 41 studies lacked outdoor surface temperature as a quantitative outcome despite reporting other thermal metrics. Twelve of the 50 eligible studies could not enter the meta-analysis due to incomplete statistical reporting, underscoring the need for standardised minimum reporting in green-wall field experiments. Cohen's κ = 0.78 indicates substantial inter-rater agreement across all screening rounds.

In (1), $\bar{X}_T$ is the mean exterior surface temperature on the green-wall (treatment) façade in °C, $\bar{X}_C$ is the mean on the matched bare reference wall in °C, $S_p$ is the pooled standard deviation across both groups, and $n_T$, $n_C$ are the sample counts (logged measurement intervals per study). The bracketed term is Hedges' small-sample correction factor — important here because 14 of the 38 quantitative studies had monitoring periods shorter than 30 days. Hedges' g was preferred over Cohen's d for that reason.

### B. Search Strategy and Screening

The search ran in Scopus, Web of Science Core Collection, and the first 200 results of Google Scholar (which returns roughly that many before relevance falls off a cliff). The Boolean string was: ("green wall" OR "living wall" OR "vertical greenery system" OR "vertical greening" OR "green façade") AND ("thermal performance" OR "cooling" OR "energy saving*" OR "surface temperature") AND ("tropical" OR "warm climate" OR "hot climate" OR "subtropical" OR "humid"). Date range: January 2010 to December 2025. We added 46 records from backward and forward citation chasing through the most-cited candidates. Inclusion required English language, peer review, original quantitative data, and a study site in Köppen A, Cwa, Cfa-warm (defined as Cfa with mean coolest-month temperature ≥ 5 °C and a CDD/HDD ratio > 1), or BSh zones.

**Table I.** Screening criteria and corresponding exclusion counts

| Criterion | Included | Excluded | n |
|---|---|---|---|
| Publication type | Peer-reviewed journal or conference | Theses, magazines, opinion pieces | 61 |
| Language | English | Other languages without translation | 23 |
| Study type | Original quantitative data | Simulation only, reviews, qualitative | 88 |
| Climate zone | Köppen A, Cwa, Cfa-warm, BSh | Other zones | 312 |
| Vertical orientation | Vertical surface only | Roof-only, horizontal | 78 |
| Full-text access | Accessible | Unavailable | 8 |

Note: The 478 records excluded at title/abstract screening (Fig. 2) correspond to the three largest categories: climate zone (312), study type (88), and vertical orientation (78). Additional filters — publication type (61), language (23), and full-text access (8) — were applied across both screening and eligibility stages, with many overlapping the three primary exclusion categories. The total excluded across all stages (duplicates 237 + screening 478 + eligibility 93 = 808) reconciles with the identification count of 858.
